//: Composite indexes for the Clarity 360 response collection.
GET /school-climate/sessions fetched EVERY document in `responses` and
filtered dates in memory, with a comment saying it did so to avoid needing a
composite index. That works at test scale and degrades forever: Firestore
bills per document read, so each dashboard refresh costs one read per answer
ever recorded, and the latency grows linearly with the product's success.
These indexes let the same queries run server-side. Deploy with:
Indexes intentionally use `ts`, the ISO-8601 STRING, not the newer `ts_at`
Timestamp. Firestore omits documents that lack an indexed field, so an index
on ts_at would silently exclude every document written before it existed --
a quieter and worse failure than the slowness being fixed. ISO-8601 sorts
lexicographically in chronological order, so string range queries are exact.
Once a backfill has given every document a ts_at, these can move.
